Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 1–4:

(p-4694) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Qasas

It was named after its containing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the narratives, he said, "Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people"﴾ [al-Qasas: 25], which indicates that whoever flees from the place of the enemies to the place of the prophets, taking heed from their stories, which indicate the salvation of the fugitives and the destruction of those who remained in the place of the enemies, is safe from destruction. This is also among the greatest aims of the Qur'an, along with its containing what other than it does not contain of the accounts of Musa. Al-Mahayimi conveyed this.

The surah is entirely Meccan. It was said that the exception is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ [al-Qasas: 52] up to His saying ﴿the ignorant﴾ [al-Qasas: 55]. Al-Tabarani related from Ibn 'Abbas that it, and the end of al-Hadid, were revealed concerning the companions of the Negus who came and witnessed the battle of Uhud.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an﴾ [al-Qasas: 85], the verse, is (said to be) because of what has been narrated of its revelation at al-Juhfah during the Hijrah to Madinah. And Allah knows best. It has eighty-eight verses, by consensus.

(p-4695) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–4] ﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾ ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ [al-Qasas: 2] ﴿We recite to you from the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth for a people who believe﴾ [al-Qasas: 3] ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn exalted himself in the land and made its people factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters﴾ [al-Qasas: 4]

﴿Ta-Sin-Mim⁠﴾: the discussion of these letters has preceded more than once. ﴿These are the verses of the clear Book﴾ [al-Qasas: 2] ﴿We recite to you from the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth for a people who believe﴾ [al-Qasas: 3]: i.e., We read to you, through the mediation of the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), a recitation mingled with truth, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We relate to you the best of narratives﴾ [Yusuf: 3]. Then He resumed with what serves as an explanation of the summarized promise, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn exalted himself in the land﴾ [al-Qasas: 4], i.e., he was arrogant and exceeded the limit in tyranny, in the land of Egypt. ﴿And made its people factions﴾ [al-Qasas: 4], i.e., groups and types, in his subjugation and obedience. ﴿Oppressing a group among them﴾ [al-Qasas: 4], and they are the Children of Israel. ﴿Slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive﴾ [al-Qasas: 4]: this was the killing of their men and the reduction of their numbers, lest they multiply and contend with him for the kingship. ﴿Indeed, he was of the corrupters﴾ [al-Qasas: 4], i.e., those firmly established in corruption and in subduing the servants.

Then Allah, exalted is He, pointed to the relief He had appointed for that group, by His saying:

(p-4696) On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[5–8] ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors﴾ ﴿and to establish them in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they feared﴾ [al-Qasas: 6] ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses: "Suckle him, and when you fear for him, then cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers."﴾ [al-Qasas: 7] ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up so that he would become for them an enemy and a grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts were ever committing sin.﴾ [al-Qasas: 8]

﴿And We wished to bestow favour﴾, i.e., We would show grace; ﴿upon those who were oppressed in the land and to make them leaders﴾, i.e., they would be followed in religion after having been subservient followers; ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾, i.e., of the kingdom of their enemy. As He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed﴾ [al-A'raf: 137], up to His saying: ﴿what they were building﴾ [al-A'raf: 137]. ﴿And to establish them in the land﴾ [al-Qasas: 6], i.e., by exercising authority over it as kings do. ﴿And to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them﴾ [al-Qasas: 6], i.e., from those oppressed people, ﴿that which they feared﴾ [al-Qasas: 6], i.e., their destruction and the loss of their kingdom, as a recompense for their corruption, their failure to reform, and their tyranny. ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses﴾ [al-Qasas: 7], i.e., right after his birth in that severe hardship: ﴿to suckle him, and when you fear for him﴾ [al-Qasas: 7], i.e., from those slaughterers who held sharpened blades to shed those pure souls; ﴿then cast him into the river﴾ [al-Qasas: 7], i.e., into the sea, which is the Nile; ﴿and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]. ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up (p-4697) so that he would become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8], i.e., that their destruction would come at his hands.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). Its complement is presented in the form of a cause, namely their picking him up, likening it in its outcome to the purpose that motivates the action. ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts were ever committing sin﴾ [al-Qasas: 8], i.e., they were criminals, so Allah punished them by raising up their enemy, the very one who would be the cause of their destruction at their own hands.

The Explanation of His Words, the Exalted:

﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said, "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son," while they did not perceive﴾ [al-Qasas: 9] ﴿And the heart of the mother of Moses became empty. Indeed, she was about to disclose him, had We not steadied her heart so that she would be among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 10] ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him," so she observed him from afar, while they did not perceive﴾ [al-Qasas: 11]

﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said﴾, i.e., to Pharaoh, when she took him out of the chest: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son, while they did not perceive﴾, i.e., what would come to pass. ﴿And the heart of the mother of Moses became empty﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], i.e., void of reason (ʿaql), because of the overwhelming distress that befell her, and her reason was carried off by consternation when news reached her that he had fallen into the hand of Pharaoh. ﴿Indeed, she was about to disclose him﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], i.e., his matter and his story, and that he was her son. ﴿Had We not steadied her heart so that she would be among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], i.e., had We not inspired her with patience. It is likened to tying up something that is slipping away, so that it becomes steady and calm. The meaning of ﴿among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 10] is: among those who affirm the promise of God, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you﴾ [al-Qasas: 7].

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is also possible that her heart became empty of worry when she heard that Pharaoh had taken a liking to him and adopted him. ﴿She was about to disclose that he was her son﴾, because she could not control herself from joy and delight at what she had heard. ﴿Had We not strengthened her heart and calmed her anxiety, which arose from the intensity of joy and elation, so that she would be among the believers who are certain of God's promise, not of Pharaoh's adoption and fondness﴾. ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him"﴾ [al-Qasas: 11], i.e., follow his trail so that you may learn his news. ﴿So she observed him from afar﴾ [al-Qasas: 11], with the letter nūn (in "junub") pronounced with a dammah or with a sukūn; i.e., from a distance. ﴿While they did not perceive﴾ [al-Qasas: 11], i.e., that she was finding out his condition.

The Explanation of His Words, the Exalted:

﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said, "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son," while they did not perceive﴾ [al-Qasas: 9] ﴿And the heart of the mother of Moses became empty. Indeed, she was about to disclose him, had We not steadied her heart so that she would be among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 10] ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him," so she observed him from afar, while they did not perceive﴾ [al-Qasas: 11]

﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said﴾, i.e., to Pharaoh, when she took him out of the chest: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son, while they did not perceive﴾, i.e., what would come to pass. ﴿And the heart of the mother of Moses became empty﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], i.e., void of reason (ʿaql), because of the overwhelming distress that befell her, and her reason was carried off by consternation when news reached her that he had fallen into the hand of Pharaoh. ﴿Indeed, she was about to disclose him﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], i.e., his matter and his story, and that he was her son. ﴿Had We not steadied her heart so that she would be among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], i.e., had We not inspired her with patience. The meaning of ﴿among the believers﴾ [al-Qasas: 10] is: among those who affirm the promise of God, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you﴾ [al-Qasas: 7].

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 28, verses 12–17:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[12–17] ﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses from before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will nurse him for you while they are sincere toward him?" So We returned him to his mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve and would know that the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Qasas: 13] ﴿And when he reached his maturity and was fully grown, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ [al-Qasas: 14] ﴿And he entered the city at a time of unawareness of its people, and he found therein two men fighting, one from his own faction and the other from his enemy. So the one from his faction called him for help against the one from his enemy, and Musa struck him with his fist and ended his life. He said, "This is from the work of Shaytan. Indeed, he is a misleading, manifest enemy."﴾ [al-Qasas: 15] ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me." And He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Qasas: 16] ﴿He said, "My Lord, for that which You have bestowed upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals."﴾ [al-Qasas: 17]

﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses from before﴾, meaning: before the account of his sister tracing his trail. The word (al-maraḍi') (wet-nurses) is the plural of (murḍi'), with a ḍammah on the mim and a kasrah on the ḍad, and it refers to the woman who nurses. The (tā') (ta-marbutah) was omitted because the term is specific to women. Or it is the plural of (marḍi') with a fatḥah on the mim, a mīmī verbal noun (maṣdar), pluralized because its roots are many. Or it is the name of the place of nursing, namely the breast. ﴿So she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will nurse him for you while they are sincere toward him?"﴾, meaning: in his nursing and rearing. ﴿So We returned him to his mother that her eye might be comforted﴾ [al-Qasas: 13], meaning: by seeing him. ﴿And she would not grieve﴾ [al-Qasas: 13], meaning: by his separation. ﴿And would know that the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Qasas: 13]. ﴿And when he reached his maturity﴾ [al-Qasas: 14], meaning: the completion of his strength. ﴿And was fully grown﴾ [al-Qasas: 14], meaning: his temperament became balanced. ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge, and thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Qasas: 14], meaning: in their deeds.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained from the account of him, peace be upon him, what gradually led to what was decreed for him of prophethood, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And he entered the city﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: Egypt, coming from the palace of Pharaoh. ﴿At a time of unawareness of its people﴾ [al-Qasas: 15]. It was said: at the time of the midday rest (al-qaylulah). And it was said: between the two evening prayers. ﴿And he found therein two men fighting﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: quarrelling. ﴿This one﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: the one, ﴿from his faction﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: from those who support him in his religion, and they are the Children of Israel. ﴿And this one﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: the other, ﴿from his enemy﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: the one who opposed him in his religion, and they are the Qibt (Copts). ﴿So the one from his faction called him for help﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: he asked him for aid. ﴿Against the one from his enemy﴾ [al-Qasas: 15] because he was wronged, and the other was wrongdoing. Aiding the wronged is obligatory, so his aid became obligatory from two aspects. ﴿Musa struck him with his fist﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: he struck him with the gathered palm of his hand. ﴿And ended his life﴾ [al-Qasas: 15], meaning: he killed him. ﴿He said, "This is from the work of Shaytan. Indeed, he is a misleading, manifest enemy"﴾ [al-Qasas: 15]. This indicates his regret over what his blow led to, namely his killing of him. He called it a wrong and sought forgiveness for it in relation to his station. ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself"﴾ [al-Qasas: 16], meaning: by killing him. ﴿So forgive me." And He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Qasas: 16].

﴿He said, "My Lord, for that which You have bestowed upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals"﴾ [al-Qasas: 17]. It is permissible that this be an oath, whose answer is omitted, meaning: "I swear by Your bestowing upon me forgiveness, I will indeed repent and will not support the criminals." And it is permissible that it be a plea for compassion, as if he said: "My Lord, protect me by the right of what You have bestowed upon me of forgiveness. So I will never be, if You protect me, a supporter of the criminals." By their support he meant either accompanying Pharaoh, joining his circle and increasing his numbers, or supporting those whose support leads to sin and wrongdoing, like the support of the Israelite which led to the killing that was not lawful for him. This is what al-Zamakhshari said.

Al-Nasir said: Indeed, he, peace be upon him, disavowed a great thing, because the supporter of the criminals is their partner in what they are engaged in. (p-4700) It is related that it will be said on the Day of Resurrection: "Where are the wrongdoers and the helpers of the wrongdoers?" They will be brought, even the one who mended a pen for them or sharpened a quill for them, and they will be placed in a coffin of iron and cast into the Fire.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 24–25:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24–25] ﴿So he watered their flock for them, then withdrew to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ ﴿Then one of the two women came to him, walking shyly. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wages for having watered [the flock] for us." And when he came to him and related to him the narrative, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."﴾ [al-Qasas: 25]

(p-4702) ﴿So he watered their flock for them﴾, i.e., he watered their sheep for their sake, without any wage. ﴿Then withdrew to the shade﴾, i.e., the shade that was there, because of the intensity of the heat. ﴿And said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need"﴾, i.e., in want. The word khayr (good) is more general than wealth, or strength, or food. Most commentators, relying on the context, understood it in the last sense. ﴿Then one of the two women came to him, walking shyly. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wages for having watered [the flock] for us." And when he came to him and related to him the narrative﴾ [al-Qasas: 25], i.e., he informed him of everything that had happened to him up until his departure, when they had conspired to kill him. ﴿He said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people"﴾ [al-Qasas: 25], i.e., by leaving beyond the limit of their authority, since they have no power in our land.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26–28] ﴿One of the two women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years. But if you complete ten, it is from you. And I do not want to burden you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous."﴾ [al-Qasas: 27] ﴿He said, "That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfil, there shall be no transgression against me. And God is Witness over what we say."﴾ [al-Qasas: 28]

﴿One of the two women said, "O my father, hire him﴾, meaning: make him your hired worker to tend your flock, for he is worthy of that. ﴿Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one﴾, meaning: the best one you could wish to employ as a worker is the one who is strong for the work and trusted in it.

Al-Zamakhshari (d. 538 AH) said: Her saying, ﴿Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one﴾, is a wise and comprehensive statement that cannot be improved upon. For when these two qualities, I mean sufficiency and trustworthiness, are combined in the one who attends to your affair, your concern is relieved and your aim is achieved. She has dispensed with saying, "Hire him for his strength and his trustworthiness," by sending forth this statement, whose context is that of a proverb and wisdom. End of quotation.

Al-Nasir said: This is also more graceful in the praise of women for men than explicit praise, and more preserving of modesty, especially if she understood that her father, peace be upon him, intended to marry her to him. How excellent is what al-Faruq (may God be pleased with him) drew from this meaning when he said: "I complain to God of the weakness of the trustworthy and the treachery of the strong." So in the content of this complaint is a request to God, exalted is He, to bless him with one who combines the two qualities, being both strong and trustworthy, whom he could rely on in what he was intent upon, may God be pleased with him. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 29–31:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 32–35:**

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[32–35] ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white, without harm. And draw your arm close to you against fear. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, I killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾ [al-Qasas: 33] ﴿And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me."﴾ [al-Qasas: 34] (p-4705) ﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so they will not reach you. By Our signs, you two and whoever follows you will be the victors."﴾ [al-Qasas: 35]

﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾, i.e., put it into it. ﴿It will come out white, without harm﴾, i.e., without defect. ﴿And draw your arm close to you﴾, i.e., your hand. ﴿Against fear﴾, i.e., dread. It is read with two fatḥas (فَتْحَتَيْنِ), two ḍammas (ضَمَّتَيْنِ), fatḥa and sukūn (فَتْحٍ وسُكُونٍ), and ḍamma and sukūn (ضَمٍّ وسُكُونٍ). (Fatḥa is the short vowel "a"; ḍamma is the short vowel "u"; sukūn is the marker of a consonant without a vowel.)

Ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarir said: it refers to what befell you of fear from the serpent. Ibn Kathir said: the apparent meaning is more general than this, namely that he (peace be upon him) was commanded, whenever he feared something, to press his hand to himself, and when he did so, what he found of fear would leave him. Perhaps someone may use this, as an act of following, by placing his hand on his heart, and what he finds will depart from him or lessen, God willing. And in Him is trust.

﴿Those two﴾ refers to the staff and the hand: ﴿are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, I killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾ [al-Qasas: 33] ﴿And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., so he will be better at explanation. He cannot bear that unless he is charged with the same as I have been charged with. ﴿So send him with me as a helper﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., one who assists. ﴿To confirm me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., for the vigor of my heart. ﴿Indeed, I fear that they will deny me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., that they will agree together to deny me, which would lead to all kinds of harm.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the benefit in his confirming his brother? I say: the purpose of his confirming him is not that he should say to him, "You have spoken truly," or say to the people, "Moses has spoken truly." Rather, it is that he should set forth the truth with his tongue, expand upon the speech concerning it, and dispute with the disbelievers with it, as the eloquent man of wit does. That functions as a confirmation that is beneficial, just as one confirms speech with proof. Do you not see His words: ﴿My brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I, so send him with me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34]? The excellence of eloquence is only needed for that, not for his saying "you have spoken truly." For Sahban and Baqil would be equal in that. Or he joins the wing of his speech to clarity, until the one who fears his denial confirms him. So he attributed the confirmation to Aaron, because he was the cause of it, as a metaphorical attribution. End of quotation.

﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother"﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], i.e., We will reinforce you with him and help you.

Al-Shihab said: Shadd (شَدّ) is strengthening, and ʿaḍud (عَضُد) is the upper arm of the hand, which is well known. So it is either a figurative allusive metonymy (كِنايَةٌ تَلْوِيحِيَّةٌ) for strengthening him, because the hand is made firm by the firmness of the upper arm, and the whole body is made firm by the firmness of the hand, and there is no barrier to the literal meaning as some have imagined. Or it is an illustrative metaphor (اسْتِعارَةٌ تَمْثِيلِيَّةٌ): the state of Moses in being strengthened by his brother, peace be upon them both, is likened to the state of the hand in being strengthened by a strong hand. ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], i.e., dominance and awe in their hearts, or proof. ﴿So they will not reach you﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], i.e., with harm, let alone killing. ﴿By Our signs﴾ [al-Qasas: 35] is connected to a deleted element, i.e., "go with Our signs." Or it is connected to "We will give" (نَجْعَلُ), i.e., We will empower you through them. Or it has the sense of "they will not reach" (لا يَصِلُونَ), i.e., you will be protected from them by them. Or it is an oath, whose answer is the omitted "they will not reach." Or it is a complement to "the victors" (الغالِبُونَ) in His words: ﴿you two and whoever follows you, the victors﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], and its being placed first is either for the sake of the rhyme (الفاصِلَةِ) or for restriction (لِلْحَصْرِ), i.e., the victors over them, even if they overcome you and overcame the worlds before you.

It is read with two fatḥas (فَتْحَتَيْنِ), two ḍammas (ضَمَّتَيْنِ), fatḥa and sukūn (فَتْحٍ وسُكُونٍ), and ḍamma and sukūn (ضَمٍّ وسُكُونٍ). (Fatḥa is the short vowel "a"; ḍamma is the short vowel "u"; sukūn is the marker of a consonant without a vowel.)

Ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarir said: it refers to what befell you of fear from the serpent. Ibn Kathir said: the apparent meaning is more general than this, namely that he (peace be upon him) was commanded, whenever he feared something, to press his hand to himself, and when he did so, what he found of fear would leave him. Perhaps someone may use this, as an act of following, by placing his hand on his heart, and what he finds will depart from him or lessen, God willing. And in Him is trust.

﴿Those two﴾ refers to the staff and the hand: ﴿are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, I killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾ [al-Qasas: 33] ﴿And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., so he will be better at explanation. He cannot bear that unless he is charged with the same as I have been charged with. ﴿So send him with me as a helper﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., one who assists. ﴿To confirm me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., for the vigor of my heart. ﴿Indeed, I fear that they will deny me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34], i.e., that they will agree together to deny me, which would lead to all kinds of harm.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, what is the benefit in his confirming his brother? I say: the purpose of his confirming him is not that he should say to him, "You have spoken truly," or say to the people, "Moses has spoken truly." Rather, it is that he should set forth the truth with his tongue, expand upon the speech concerning it, and dispute with the disbelievers with it, as the eloquent man of wit does. That functions as a confirmation that is beneficial, just as one confirms speech with proof. Do you not see His words: ﴿My brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in speech than I, so send him with me﴾ [al-Qasas: 34]? The excellence of eloquence is only needed for that, not for his saying "you have spoken truly." For Sahban and Baqil would be equal in that. Or he joins the wing of his speech to clarity, until the one who fears his denial confirms him. So he attributed the confirmation to Aaron, because he was the cause of it, as a metaphorical attribution. End of quotation.

﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother"﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], i.e., We will reinforce you with him and help you.

Al-Shihab said: Shadd (شَدّ) is strengthening, and ʿaḍud (عَضُد) is the upper arm of the hand, which is well known. So it is either a figurative allusive metonymy (كِنايَةٌ تَلْوِيحِيَّةٌ) for strengthening him, because the hand is made firm by the firmness of the upper arm, and the whole body is made firm by the firmness of the hand, and there is no barrier to the literal meaning as some have imagined. Or it is an illustrative metaphor (اسْتِعارَةٌ تَمْثِيلِيَّةٌ): the state of Moses in being strengthened by his brother, peace be upon them both, is likened to the state of the hand in being strengthened by a strong hand. ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], i.e., dominance and awe in their hearts, or proof. ﴿So they will not reach you﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], i.e., with harm, let alone killing. ﴿By Our signs﴾ [al-Qasas: 35] is connected to a deleted element, i.e., "go with Our signs." Or it is connected to "We will give" (نَجْعَلُ), i.e., We will empower you through them. Or it has the sense of "they will not reach" (لا يَصِلُونَ), i.e., you will be protected from them by them. Or it is an oath, whose answer is the omitted "they will not reach." Or it is a complement to "the victors" (الغالِبُونَ) in His words: ﴿you two and whoever follows you, the victors﴾ [al-Qasas: 35], and its being placed first is either for the sake of the rhyme (الفاصِلَةِ) or for restriction (لِلْحَصْرِ), i.e., the victors over them, even if they overcome you and overcame the worlds before you.

The discussion of the Lord's words, the Exalted:

[36–38] ﴿So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, "This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we have not heard of this among our forefathers, the earlier ones."﴾ ﴿Moses said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and who will have the final outcome of the abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 37] ﴿Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a lofty tower that I may look upon the God of Moses, though I think he is among the liars."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38]

﴿So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, "This is nothing but fabricated magic"﴾: that is, invented, with no precedent for it. Or [it means] you forged it against God by attributing it to Him, while you learned it from others. Thus "fabrication" (iftira') means fabrication (ikhtilaq) or lying. ﴿And we have not heard of this﴾: that is, of this magic, or of the claim to prophethood, or that the world has a God who sends messengers with signs (p-4707) ﴿among our forefathers, the earlier ones﴾: that is, existing in their times.

Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: This is either a deliberate lie and obstinacy, denying the prophethoods, even though the time of Joseph was near to them; or because they did not believe in him either.

﴿Moses said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and who will have the final outcome of the abode"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 37]. Al-Mahayimi said: Its meaning is: it is sufficient as proof that these are signs, that they are extraordinary acts (kharq) with no precedent. Moreover, what I have brought is guidance, and the magician in general does not call to guidance. If you do not acknowledge that it is guidance, then my Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and He knows this by the outcome, for God will surely make the end of the people of guidance good. For He knows who will have the final outcome of the abode, which is the praiseworthy end. The "abode" refers to this world. Its outcome and its final result (ʿuqbā) is that the servant is sealed with mercy and good pleasure, and the angels greet him with glad tidings at death. This will not be the lot of a magician who claims prophethood, because he is a wrongdoer, so he will not succeed in the praiseworthy end, as He said: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ [Al-Qasas: 37], that is, in the abode, even if they attain some of their aims at first through gradual lure (istidraj). So they do not win the praiseworthy final outcome. Their ultimate fate is only the cutting off of their trace and an evil remembrance. God has indeed fulfilled this promise, making the end of the people of Moses exalted and the end of his enemies abased.

﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38]. This relates his rebellion, his arrogance and his tyranny in uttering that monstrous statement. Just as he confronted Moses with it in his saying: ﴿He said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned"﴾ [Al-Shu'ara: 29]. And as God, the Exalted, said of him: ﴿Then he gathered [his people] and called out﴾ [Al-Nazi'at: 23], ﴿and said, "I am your lord, the Most High"﴾ [Al-Nazi'at: 24], ﴿so God seized him in the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾ [Al-Nazi'at: 25], ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾ [Al-Nazi'at: 26]. That is, he gathered his people and called out among them, proclaiming this openly. So He took revenge upon him by making him a lesson for whoever takes heed.

﴿So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38]: that is, a fire, so that I may make bricks from it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He did not say, "Bake the bricks for me and make them," because this expression is more harmonious (tibaq) with the eloquence of the Qur'an and its elevated level, and more fitting to the speech of tyrants. Haman was his vizier and the manager of his subjects. ﴿Then make for me﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38]: that is, from the bricks, ﴿a lofty tower﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38]: that is, a high palace reaching toward the sky, ﴿that I may look upon the God of Moses﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38] (p-4708) meaning the Most High, the Exalted, blessed and exalted is He. ﴿Though I think he is among the liars﴾ [Al-Qasas: 38]: that is, in his claim to divinity and to being exalted over the Creator of the earth and the heavens.

**Commentary of al-Qāsimī (Maḥāsin al-Ta'wīl, "The Beauties of Interpretation") on Sūrah al-Qaṣaṣ, verses 39–43:**

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wīl*, the deeper explanation of meaning) of His saying, exalted is He:

[39–43] ﴿And he (Pharaoh) and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.﴾ ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 40] ﴿And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 41] ﴿And We followed them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42] ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the previous generations, as evidence (*baṣā'ir*) for the people and guidance and mercy, that they might remember.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43]

﴿And he was arrogant﴾, i.e., by claiming divinity for himself, denying it of Allah, exalted is He, intending to look upon Allah, may He be glorified, and claiming total sovereignty for himself while ignorant of his Lord. ﴿And his soldiers in the land without right﴾, i.e., rather by corruption, rejection of the truth, and turning people away from the way of Allah. ﴿And they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾: the verb *yurja'ūn* is read in two ways, with a *ḍammah* on the *yā'* and with a *fatḥah* on it. ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 40]. ﴿And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 41]. ﴿And We followed them in this world with a curse﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42], i.e., every believer who hears of them curses them. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42], i.e., among the expelled and the distanced. ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., lights for the hearts. ﴿And guidance﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., to the correct beliefs and their proofs. ﴿And mercy﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., by guiding to righteous action. ﴿That they might remember﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., that they may be admonished by it and be guided through it.

(p-4709) Then Allah, exalted is He, pointed to the fact that the revelation is inspiration from the All-Knower of the unseen, by explaining that these detailed accounts could not be known except through direct observation or learning, and both of these are known to be absent. Thus the truthfulness of the revelation is established. This is His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wīl*, the deeper explanation of meaning) of His saying, exalted is He:

[39–43] ﴿And he (Pharaoh) and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.﴾ ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 40] ﴿And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 41] ﴿And We followed them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42] ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the previous generations, as evidence (*baṣā'ir*) for the people and guidance and mercy, that they might remember.﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43]

﴿And he was arrogant﴾, i.e., by claiming divinity for himself, denying it of Allah, exalted is He, intending to look upon Allah, may He be glorified, and claiming total sovereignty for himself while ignorant of his Lord. ﴿And his soldiers in the land without right﴾, i.e., rather by corruption, rejection of the truth, and turning people away from the way of Allah. ﴿And they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾: the verb *yurja'ūn* is read in two ways, with a *ḍammah* on the *yā'* and with a *fatḥah* on it. ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 40]. ﴿And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 41]. ﴿And We followed them in this world with a curse﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42], i.e., every believer who hears of them curses them. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42], i.e., among the expelled and the distanced. ﴿And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., lights for the hearts. ﴿And guidance﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., to the correct beliefs and their proofs. ﴿And mercy﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., by guiding to righteous action. ﴿That they might remember﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 43], i.e., that they may be admonished by it and be guided through it.

(p-4709) Then Allah, exalted is He, pointed to the fact that the revelation is inspiration from the All-Knower of the unseen, by explaining that these detailed accounts could not be known except through direct observation or learning, and both of these are known to be absent. Thus the truthfulness of the revelation is established. This is His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 44–46:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44–46] ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿But We produced generations, and the lifetime grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were sending [messengers].﴾ [al-Qasas: 45] ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called [Moses], but [it is] a mercy from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they may remember.﴾ [al-Qasas: 46]

﴿And you were not on the western side﴾ i.e., the western valley where Moses was given the revelation of the secret conversation. ﴿When We decreed﴾ i.e., We determined and ended, ﴿to Moses the command﴾ i.e., the command of sending and informing. ﴿Nor were you among the witnesses.﴾ ﴿But We produced generations﴾ [al-Qasas: 45] i.e., between your time and the time of Moses. ﴿And the lifetime grew long for them﴾ [al-Qasas: 45] i.e., the period of the cessation of revelation was extended, the landmarks of guidance were effaced, and misguidance, oppression and perdition spread widely, so Our mercy required sending you to bring them out of the darknesses into the light. ﴿And you were not dwelling﴾ [al-Qasas: 45] i.e., residing, ﴿among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses﴾ [al-Qasas: 45] i.e., to you, and revealing those verses to you. That is, the reporting of them was only by revelation whose source is the Message. ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called﴾ [al-Qasas: 46] i.e., at the time of Our calling Moses. ﴿But [it is] a mercy from your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas: 46] i.e., but We sent you with the Qur'an, which speaks of what was mentioned and of other things, as a great mercy from Us to you and to mankind. ﴿That you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾ [al-Qasas: 46] i.e., no warner in the period of the interval (fatra) between you and Jesus. ﴿That they may remember﴾ [al-Qasas: 46] i.e., that they may take heed by your warning.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 28, verses 47–48:**

[p-4710] The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[47–48] ﴿Had it not been that a calamity should afflict them for what their hands have sent forth, and they say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two magicians supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾ [al-Qasas: 48]

﴿Had it not been that a calamity should afflict them﴾, i.e., a punishment, ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾, i.e., of disbelief and corruption, ﴿and they say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾, i.e., by them. The response to the first ﴿Had it not been (lawla)﴾ is omitted, relying on the circumstances to indicate it, i.e., "We would not have sent you." However, their saying this at the time of their punishment is certain. Therefore We sent you, to cut off their excuses.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Since most actions are carried out by the hands, every action came to be expressed by the committing (ijtiraḥ) and the sending forth of the hands, even if it is an action of the hearts. This is a broadening of speech, making the lesser follow the greater and giving precedence to the greater over the lesser. ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?"﴾, i.e., such as the turning of the staff into a serpent, the splitting of the sea, and other signs, out of obstinacy and stubbornness, just as they said: ﴿Why has no treasure been sent down to him, or why has no angel come with him?﴾ [Hud: 12], and what is similar to that. His words ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?﴾ are a refutation of them and a demonstration that what they said was pure obstinacy, not a seeking of what would guide them to the truth. That is: did not the people of their own kind disbelieve, those whose way is their way and whose stubbornness is their stubbornness, namely the al-Qibt (Copts), in what was given to Moses of the Book? ﴿They said﴾ [al-Qasas: 48], i.e., concerning Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them both: ﴿"Two magicians supporting each other"﴾ [al-Qasas: 48], i.e., assisting one another. It is also read as "siḥrān" (sihran), meaning "possessors of two magics", or they made them two instances of magic for emphasis. ﴿And they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾ [al-Qasas: 48]

Then the Exalted indicated that the greatest sign for the Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, is the inner, cognitive signs, not the cosmic, horizontal signs that were given to others, in keeping with the law of progression. For when Islam came, the human species had become prepared to know truth from falsehood through proof, and to distinguish good from evil through evidence and argument. In this stage it necessarily needed a teacher and guide, as in the other stages. So Allah sent to it a messenger who would guide it to the paths of reflection and inference, and who would command it to reject mere blind imitation and unthinking submission, and not to accept anything except by evidence and proof that leads to knowledge. Thus the foundation of his, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, argument for the proof of his prophethood and messengership was his noble self and what he brought of light and guidance, like the physician whose skill in the medical art is inferred from the knowledge and successful practice he displays in it. This has been expounded in its proper places. This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He:

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

**[49–55]** ﴿Say: "Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guidance than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 50] ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word, that they may be reminded.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 51] ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 52] ﴿And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims [submitting] before it."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 53] ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54] (p-4712) ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55]

﴿Say﴾, i.e., to these deniers: The era of the extraordinary signs you propose has passed. Allah, Exalted is He, has abrogated (naskh) those signs by bringing something better than them, namely the sign of guidance by which the hearts of all the worlds are set right, and the reminder that restrains souls from evil and moves them toward good, such that its good effect appears among the believers, while misery is made due for the deniers and the obstinate. So if this is sorcery, then you have something better in guidance: ﴿Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guidance than these two﴾, i.e., than the Torah and the Qur'an. ﴿I will follow it﴾, i.e., and I will not be obstinate with you as you are obstinate with me. ﴿If you are truthful﴾, i.e., in your claim that the two are fabricated sorcery, or in your claim that it is possible to produce something better in guidance than them.

Abu al-Su'ud said: A condition of this kind is used by one who relies on the clarity of his proof and the manifest nature of his way, because bringing something better than the two Books is manifestly impossible. Thus it broadens the scope of speech for rebuke and silencing. End of quote. I.e., it is not [meant] for doubt and hesitation.

Al-Shihab said: This is an answer to the objection that their failure to bring such a book is already known. This is like one who says, with confidence: "If I am your old friend, then treat me with ignorance." Likewise, the use of the particle ''in'' (if) alongside the impossibility of their truthfulness conveys a kind of mockery of them. ﴿And if they do not respond to you﴾ [Al-Qasas: 50], i.e., if they do not bring that Book and do not follow the two Books: ﴿then know that they only follow their own desires﴾ [Al-Qasas: 50], i.e., their deviant desires without proof. ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah﴾ [Al-Qasas: 50]. The interrogative is a denial of the negation: i.e., no one is more astray than him. How could it not be so? For he is the most unjust of the unjust, by preferring his desire over the guidance of Allah, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-Qasas: 50], i.e., those who wronged themselves by immersing themselves in following desire and turning away from the signs that guide to the clear truth.

(p-4713) Al-Razi said: This is among the greatest proofs of the corruption of blind imitation (taqlid), and that proof and argument are necessary. End of quote.

﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word﴾ [Al-Qasas: 51], i.e., We sent down the Qur'an to them in continuous succession, one part following another, containing promise and warning, stories and lessons, and admonitions, as wisdom and benefit require, in order that they might be reminded and thus prosper. It is read ''wassalna'' with shaddah (intensive) and without it.

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it﴾ [Al-Qasas: 52], i.e., the Qur'an. ﴿They believe in it﴾ [Al-Qasas: 52], and they are the believers among the People of the Book and their allies. ﴿And when it is recited to them﴾ [Al-Qasas: 53], i.e., the Qur'an. ﴿They say, "We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before its descent, Muslims"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 53], i.e., before its revelation, ﴿Muslims﴾ [Al-Qasas: 53], i.e., submitting to it, because of the good tidings of it that we had. Or [it means] upon the religion of Islam, which is sincerely turning one's face to Allah, Exalted is He, without associating anything with Him. ﴿Those﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54], i.e., those described with the attributes mentioned, ﴿will be given their reward twice﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54], meaning once for their belief in their own Book, and once for their belief in the Qur'an. ﴿For what they patiently endured﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54], i.e., for their patience and steadfastness in both beliefs. Or [it means] for believing in the Qur'an before its descent and after it. Or for enduring the harm of those who opposed them. ﴿And they repel﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54], i.e., they push away ﴿evil with good﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54], i.e., with good wisdom, what would harm them. ﴿And they spend from what We have provided them﴾ [Al-Qasas: 54], i.e., upon the needy and the poor, and in the way of righteousness and goodness, fleeing from the stain of miserliness and being mindful of its harms.

﴿And when they hear vain talk﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55], i.e., from the ignorant. It is everything that ought to be discarded and left aside, of foolishness and other things. ﴿They turn away from it﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55], i.e., honoring themselves by avoiding association with the base, and honoring their hearing by not taking in their worthless falsehood. ﴿And they say﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55], i.e., to them: ﴿For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55], i.e., as a farewell and a parting. It is reported from al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him): this is the word of the forbearance of the believers. ﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55], i.e., we do not desire their company or companionship, nor do we desire to repay their falsehood with falsehood. Al-Razi said: Some people said this was abrogated by the command to fight. But this is far-fetched, because abandoning futile abuse is recommended, even though fighting is obligatory. End of quote.

**Note:**

Ibn Kathir reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: These verses were revealed concerning seventy of the priests (qissisin) whom the Negus (al-Najashi) had sent. When they came to the Prophet ﷺ, he recited to them: ﴿Ya-Sin﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1] ﴿By the wise Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin: 2], until he finished it. Then they began to weep, and they embraced Islam.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in (the Sirah): Then there came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was in Makkah, twenty men or thereabouts of the Christians, when news of him had reached them from Abyssinia. They found him in the mosque, so they sat with him, spoke with him, and questioned him. Men of Quraysh were in their assemblies around the Ka'bah. When they had finished questioning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about what they wanted, he called them to Allah, Exalted is He, and recited the Qur'an to them. When they heard the Qur'an, their eyes overflowed with tears. Then they responded to Allah, believed in Him, affirmed him, and recognized in him what had been described to them in their Book concerning his matter. The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil, explanation of meaning) of His saying, exalted is He:

[59–62] ﴿Your Lord would never destroy the cities until He had sent to their mother-town a messenger reciting Our verses to them. Will you not reason?﴾ [al-Qasas: 60] ﴿Is one to whom We have made a good promise, and who will encounter it, like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, and who on the Day of Resurrection will be among those brought forward?﴾ [al-Qasas: 61] ﴿And on the Day when He calls to them and says: "Where are My associates whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 62]

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 63–68 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[63–68] ﴿Those against whom the Word has been justified will say: "Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray. We led them astray just as we ourselves went astray. We disown them before You. They did not used to worship us."﴾ ﴿And it will be said: "Call upon your partners," so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!﴾ [28:64] ﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says: "What answer did you give to the messengers?"﴾ [28:65] ﴿Then the reports will be obscured for them that Day, and they will not question one another.﴾ [28:66] ﴿As for him who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful.﴾ [28:67] ﴿Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses. They have no choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ [28:68]

﴿Those against whom the Word has been justified will say﴾: that is, it became due and its consequence was established, namely the descent of the threat upon them. By them are meant the leaders of misguidance and the chiefs of disbelief and corruption. ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray﴾: that is, we caused them to go astray. Abu al-Su'ud said: their purpose in the gesture (of pointing) is to show that they are saying this in their presence, and that they are unable to deny or refute it. ﴿We led them astray just as we went astray﴾: that is, we misled them through whispering and embellishment, just as we went astray by our own choice and by preferring what perishes over what endures. ﴿We disown them before You﴾: that is, from disbelief, polytheism and sins; or from them and from what they chose. ﴿They did not used to worship us﴾: that is, rather they used to worship [p. 4719] their own desires and appetites.

﴿And it will be said: "Call upon your partners"﴾ [28:64]: so that they may intercede for you. ﴿So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!﴾ [28:64]: that is, they will wish for that so that they may be rescued from the great punishment. ﴿On the Day He calls to them and says: "What answer did you give to the messengers?"﴾ [28:65]: that is, to those who called them to guidance, to the reform of deeds and of morals. ﴿Then the reports will be obscured for them that Day﴾ [28:66]: that is, the reports become like the blind to them, unable to find their way to them. Its original form was "they became blind to the reports," but it was reversed for the sake of emphasis. Al-Shihab said: in it there is an explicit, subordinate metaphor (isti'arah). Blindness is borrowed for the lack of guidance, so they are not guided to the reports. Then it was inverted for emphasis, so that the reports are described as not finding their way to them. And the meaning of obscurity (khafa') was implied, so it is governed by ʿalā ("upon"). Thus there are several kinds of eloquence in it: metaphor, inversion (qalb) and implication (tadmin). By "the reports" is meant what they answered the messengers with, or what includes that and other things, namely every answer that could be given. ﴿So they will not question one another﴾ [28:66]: that is, they will not ask one another about the answer, because of the extreme of their bewilderment; or because each knows that the other is equally unable to answer; or because they are unable to speak, with their mouths sealed.

Then, this threat applies to the persistent: ﴿As for him who repents﴾ [28:67]: that is, from polytheism; ﴿believes and does righteous deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful﴾ [28:67]: that is, that he will attain success with Allah. The word ʿasā ("perhaps") coming from the Generous is a confirmation (of the outcome). It is also permissible that it signify the hope and longing of the penitent, as if He had said: let him hope to be among the successful. This was said by al-Zamakhshari. ﴿Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses﴾ [28:68]: that is, according to what His will and care require, He wills. ﴿They have no choice﴾ [28:68]: that is, in that matter. Rather, the choosing belongs to Him in His acts, and He knows best the aspects of wisdom in them; no one of His creation has the right to choose over Him.

So the context of these verses, if you examine it, is found to contain this meaning and to revolve around it. And Allah knows best.

Sixth: this verse is mentioned right after His saying: ﴿On the Day He calls to them and says: "What answer did you give to the messengers?"﴾ [28:65]; ﴿Then the reports will be obscured for them that Day, and they will not question one another﴾ [28:66]; ﴿As for him who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful﴾ [28:67]; ﴿Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses﴾ [28:68]. Just as He alone created them, glory be to Him, He chose from among them those who repented, believed and did righteous deeds, so they became His elite among His servants and His chosen ones from His creation. This choosing was in accordance with His wisdom and knowledge, glory be to Him, for the one who is fit for it, not according to the choice or proposal of these polytheists. So glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.

Then Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (Section) When you reflect upon the conditions of this creation, you will see that this choosing and specifying within it points to His Lordship, His Oneness, and the perfection of His wisdom, knowledge, and power. And that He is Allah, there is no god but Him, so He has no partner who creates as He creates, chooses as He chooses, or governs as He governs. This choosing, governing, and specifying, whose effect is evident in this world, is among the greatest signs of His Lordship, the greatest witnesses to His Oneness, to the attributes of His perfection, and to the truthfulness of His Messenger. We will point out from it a small amount that serves as a reminder of what lies beyond it and as an indication of what is other than it. Allah created seven heavens and chose the highest of them, making it the abode of the closest of His angels, and singled it out for proximity to His Kursi and His Throne. He settled in it whomever He willed of His creation. It therefore has a distinction and superiority over the rest of the heavens, and it would suffice that it is nearer to Him, blessed and exalted is He. This preference and specification, despite the equality of the substance of the heavens, is among the clearest proofs of the perfection of His power and wisdom, and that He creates what He wills and chooses. From this is His, glorified is He, preference of the Garden of Firdaws over the rest of the Gardens, and His singling it out by making His Throne its ceiling. In some narrations: Allah, glorified is He, planted it with His own hand and chose it for His chosen ones among His creation. From this is His choosing of the angels, those chosen from among them above the rest, such as Jibril, Mika'il, and Israfil. Likewise is His, glorified is He, choosing of the Prophets from the children of Adam, and choosing of the Messengers from among them, and choosing from among them the Messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-'azm). And His choosing of the two friends (Khalilayn), Ibrahim and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both. From this is His, glorified and exalted is He, choosing the offspring of Isma'il from among the kinds of the sons of Adam. Then He chose from them the Banu Kinanah ibn Khuzaymah. Then He chose from the offspring of Kinanah the Quraysh. Then He chose from the Quraysh the Banu Hashim. Then He chose from the Banu Hashim the master of the children of Adam, Muhammad (ﷺ). Likewise He chose his Companions from among all the worlds, and chose from among them the foremost early ones, and chose from among them the people of Badr and the people of the Pledge of al-Ridwan. He chose for them from the religion its most complete form, from the laws its best, and from the morals the purest, most wholesome, and most pure. And He chose his Ummah (ﷺ) above all the nations. From this is His, glorified and exalted is He, choosing from places and lands the best and most noble, which is the Sacred City (al-Balad al-Haram). He, glorified is He, chose it for His Prophet and made it the rites (manasik) for His servants, and made it obligatory upon them to come to it from near and far, from every deep mountain pass. They do not enter it except humble, submissive, and abased, with their heads uncovered, stripped of the clothing of the people of this world. He made it a secure sanctuary (haram) in which no blood is shed, no tree is cut, no game is startled, and its grass is not cut, and its lost property is not picked up for keeping, but only for announcing it. From this is His preference of some days and months over others. The best of days before Allah is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), which is the Day of the Greater Hajj, as in (al-Sunan). The best of months is the month of Ramadan, its last ten nights are the best nights, the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) is better than a thousand months, Friday is the best day of the week, and the Day of 'Arafah and the Day of Sacrifice are the best days of the year. End, summarized.

The reasoning and evidence have been amply presented. May Allah have mercy on him, be pleased with him, and make him content. As for His Exalted saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas: 68], meaning: exalting Allah above anyone whose choice is not contested by any other choice, ﴿and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Qasas: 68].

(p-4724) On the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted:

[69–71] ﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.﴾ ﴿And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs praise in the first [life] and the last, and to Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [al-Qasas: 70] ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah that could bring you light? Then will you not listen?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 71]

﴿And your Lord knows what they conceal﴾, i.e., hide: ﴿their breasts﴾, i.e., of deceit and scheming; ﴿and what they declare﴾, i.e., of words and deeds. ﴿And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him﴾ [al-Qasas: 70], i.e., He alone is the one deserving of divinity (ulūhiyyah) and worship. ﴿To Him belongs praise in the first [life] and the last﴾ [al-Qasas: 70], i.e., because He is the master of all blessings in both abodes. ﴿And to Him belongs the judgment﴾ [al-Qasas: 70], i.e., the executed decree over everything; He overpowers everything according to the requirement of His will, and judges concerning it by the necessity of His determination. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qasas: 70], i.e., by resurrection for recompense. ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah that could bring you light?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 71], i.e., this true statement, heard with contemplation (samā' tadabbur).

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[72–76] ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?" And of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ [al-Qasas: 72–73] ﴿And the day He will call them and say, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 74] ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness, and We will say, "Bring your proof." Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is what they used to invent.﴾ [al-Qasas: 75] ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We had given him of treasures whose keys would surely burden a company of strong men, when his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant."﴾ [al-Qasas: 76]

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?"﴾ That is: this benefit, so that you may stand in gratitude for it. ﴿And of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein﴾ [al-Qasas: 73], that is, in the night; ﴿and seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas: 73], that is, in the day; ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas: 73], that is, for His blessings, the apparent and the hidden, the bodily and the spiritual, by employing them in what obedience to Him requires. And that is in accordance with what they were created for.

﴿And the day He will call them and say, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 74] ﴿And We will extract﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, and We will bring forth, ﴿from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, a prophet who will bear witness against them concerning what they used to be upon. As in His words, Exalted Is He: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness﴾ [al-Nisa: 41]. ﴿And We will say﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, to every nation of those nations: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, for what you are upon: is it true or not? So they will all be unable. And the proof of the Prophet becomes manifest, as He, Exalted Is He, said: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, in divinity, none shares in it with Him; ﴿and lost from them﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, it vanished from them as the vanishing of what is lost; ﴿is what they used to invent﴾ [al-Qasas: 75], that is, of falsehood and the diverse doctrines and the scattered, divergent paths.

﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, of their kind in disbelief and tyranny. And the people of Moses are his community to whom he was sent, and they are the Copts and their tyrant, Pharaoh. ﴿But he oppressed them﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, through arrogance and domineering over them, when greed and love of this world overcame him, due to his delusion and his self-exaltation by seeing the adornment of himself. ﴿And We had given him of treasures﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, of wealth stored up; ﴿whose keys﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, the keys of its chests, by elision of a noun, or the idiomatic attribution for the slightest connection; and it has been said, "its treasuries." ﴿Would surely burden﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, would weigh heavily; ﴿a company﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, a large group of men or mules; ﴿of strong men, when his people said to him, "Do not exult"﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, at the ornaments of this world with an exultation that preoccupies you from giving thanks for it and from fulfilling its due; ﴿indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾ [al-Qasas: 76], that is, this exultation, because of what it contains of preferring it over the Hereafter, being content with it instead of it, and inclining towards it. And that is the root of every evil and the wellspring of every corruption.

**A Benefit:**

Regarding ﴿ويْكَأنَّ﴾ [Al-Qasas: 82] there are several opinions:

The first: that ﴿way﴾ (ويْ) is a word by itself. It is an ism fi'l (verb-like noun), meaning "I am amazed." The kāf is for causation (ta'līl), and ﴿anna﴾ (أنَّ) and what follows it are governed by it. That is, "I am amazed because Allah extends provision..." The analogy of this view is that one should pause on ﴿way﴾ alone, and al-Kisa'i did so.

The second: that it is composed of ﴿way﴾ for wonder and ﴿ka-anna﴾ (كَأنَّ) for comparison. The meaning is: "How alike is the matter that Allah extends..." That is, how alike is the affair of the world and of people in general, up to the end of the affair of Qarun and what was witnessed of his story. The "matter" is taken from the pronoun, for it refers to the matter at hand. The purpose of comparing the situation to this situation is that, because it is established and well known, anything may be compared to it, as indicated by al-Kashshaf.

The third: some have said that ﴿ka-anna﴾ here is for comparison, except that its meaning has departed from it and it has become for affirmation and certainty. This also suits pausing on ﴿way﴾.

The fourth: al-Hamdani claimed in al-Fara'id that the view of Sibawayh and al-Khalil is that ﴿way﴾ is for regret and ﴿ka-anna﴾ is for wonder. The meaning: they regretted, amazed that Allah extends provision...

Al-Shihab said: That ﴿ka-anna﴾ is for wonder is not known.

The fifth: the Kufans held that it is composed of ﴿wayka﴾ meaning ﴿waylaka﴾, which was lightened by dropping the lam. The governing element of ﴿an﴾ is the implied "know" (i'lam). The kāf in this case is a pronoun in the genitive position. This suits pausing on the kāf, and Abu 'Amr did so.

The sixth: that ﴿wayka﴾ is a word by itself, and the kāf is a particle of address. This is close to what preceded it. Abu al-Baqa' said: This is weak for two reasons: first, the meaning of address here is remote; second, the estimate of ﴿way﴾ as "know" has no parallel, and it is not permissible in every context. End of quotation.

The seventh: that ﴿wayka-anna﴾ entirely is an independent, simple word, meaning "Did you not see?" This is perhaps narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Fara' and al-Kisa'i transmitted that it means "Do you not see the handiwork of Allah?" Ibn Qutayba related that in the dialect of Himyar it means "mercy be upon you." In the Qur'an, only ﴿ويْكَأنَّ﴾ and ﴿ويْكَأنَّهُ﴾ are written joined in both places. Most readers followed the orthography. Al-Kisa'i paused on ﴿way﴾ and Abu 'Amr on ﴿wayka﴾.

This is what is derived from the glosses of al-Qadi and al-Samin. In my view, it is composed of ﴿way﴾ for wonder and ﴿ka-anna﴾ meaning certainty, which is one of its known meanings. The pause is on ﴿way﴾. The fact that it is written joined in the codices does not pose a difficulty for this, because writing, as Ibn Kathir said, is a conventional, customary matter, and the reference is to the Arabic pronunciation.

The linguists have agreed that ﴿way﴾ is an interjection of wonder. One says ﴿wayka﴾ and ﴿way li-Zayd﴾, and it enters upon the lightened ﴿ka-an﴾ and the emphatic ﴿ka-anna﴾. Of the examples of the first is the poet's saying:

"They asked me for divorce when they saw me: my wealth has become little. You have come to me with something unfamiliar.
Alas, as if the one who possesses wealth is loved, and whoever is poor lives a life of hardship."

This verse indicates what has been deduced, let alone its use down to these generations.

Ibn Kathir said: Israelite narrations have been mentioned here, which we have set aside. We followed his example, indeed we exceeded him in setting aside much of what is narrated from him, both the mawquf and the weak, with which pages have been blackened.

The kāf is for causation (ta'līl), and ﴿anna﴾ (أنَّ) and what follows it are governed by it. That is, "I am amazed because Allah extends provision..." The analogy of this view is that one should pause on ﴿way﴾ alone, and al-Kisa'i did so.

The second: that it is composed of ﴿way﴾ for wonder and ﴿ka-anna﴾ (كَأنَّ) for comparison. The meaning is: "How alike is the matter that Allah extends..." That is, how alike is the affair of the world and of people in general, up to the end of the affair of Qarun and what was witnessed of his story. The "matter" is taken from the pronoun, for it refers to the matter at hand. The purpose of comparing the situation to this situation is that, because it is established and well known, anything may be compared to it, as indicated by al-Kashshaf.

The third: some have said that ﴿ka-anna﴾ here is for comparison, except that its meaning has departed from it and it has become for affirmation and certainty. This also suits pausing on ﴿way﴾.

The fourth: al-Hamdani claimed in al-Fara'id that the view of Sibawayh and al-Khalil is that ﴿way﴾ is for regret and ﴿ka-anna﴾ is for wonder. The meaning: they regretted, amazed that Allah extends provision...

Al-Shihab said: That ﴿ka-anna﴾ is for wonder is not known.

The fifth: the Kufans held that it is composed of ﴿wayka﴾ meaning ﴿waylaka﴾, which was lightened by dropping the lam. The governing element of ﴿an﴾ is the implied "know" (i'lam). The kāf in this case is a pronoun in the genitive position. This suits pausing on the kāf, and Abu 'Amr did so.

The sixth: that ﴿wayka﴾ is a word by itself, and the kāf is a particle of address. This is close to what preceded it. Abu al-Baqa' said: This is weak for two reasons: first, the meaning of address here is remote; second, the estimate of ﴿way﴾ as "know" has no parallel, and it is not permissible in every context. End of quotation.

The seventh: that ﴿wayka-anna﴾ entirely is an independent, simple word, meaning "Did you not see?" This is perhaps narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Fara' and al-Kisa'i transmitted that it means "Do you not see the handiwork of Allah?" Ibn Qutayba related that in the dialect of Himyar it means "mercy be upon you." In the Qur'an, only ﴿ويْكَأنَّ﴾ and ﴿ويْكَأنَّهُ﴾ are written joined in both places. Most readers followed the orthography. Al-Kisa'i paused on ﴿way﴾ and Abu 'Amr on ﴿wayka﴾.

This is what is derived from the glosses of al-Qadi and al-Samin. In my view, it is composed of ﴿way﴾ for wonder and ﴿ka-anna﴾ meaning certainty, which is one of its known meanings. The pause is on ﴿way﴾. The fact that it is written joined in the codices does not pose a difficulty for this, because writing, as Ibn Kathir said, is a conventional, customary matter, and the reference is to the Arabic pronunciation.

The linguists have agreed that ﴿way﴾ is an interjection of wonder. One says ﴿wayka﴾ and ﴿way li-Zayd﴾, and it enters upon the lightened ﴿ka-an﴾ and the emphatic ﴿ka-anna﴾. Of the examples of the first is the poet's saying:

"They asked me for divorce when they saw me: my wealth has become little. You have come to me with something unfamiliar.
Alas, as if the one who possesses wealth is loved, and whoever is poor lives a life of hardship."

This verse indicates what has been deduced, let alone its use down to these generations.

Ibn Kathir said: Israelite narrations have been mentioned here, which we have set aside. We followed his example, indeed we exceeded him in setting aside much of what is narrated from him, both the mawquf and the weak, with which pages have been blackened.

Then Exalted is He pointed to the contrast between the state of Qarun and the state of His sincere servants, by His saying, Glorified is He:

**The Discussion Concerning the Interpretation of His, Exalted is He, Saying:**

﴿Then he went out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."﴾ ﴿But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteous deeds, and none is granted it except the patient."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 80] ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And he had no company to support him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 81] ﴿And by morning, those who had wished to be in his place said, "Ah! It is as if Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. Ah! It is as if the disbelievers never prosper."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 82]

﴿Then he went out﴾, i.e., Qarun, being insolent. ﴿before his people in his adornment﴾, i.e., deluded by gazing upon it. ﴿Those who desired the worldly life said﴾, i.e., following the customs of human nature, from the desire for abundance and ease: ﴿"Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."﴾ ﴿But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better﴾ [Al-Qasas: 80], i.e., than what you wish for: ﴿for one who believes and does righteous deeds, and none is granted it﴾ [Al-Qasas: 80], i.e., this statement uttered by those who had been given knowledge. Or it refers to Paradise. Or to the conduct and the way, which is faith and righteous deeds: ﴿except the patient﴾ [Al-Qasas: 80], i.e., those who are patient in acts of obedience and in restraining desires, and who keep their souls on a leash so that they do not follow adornments.

﴿Woe to you﴾ (wayla-ka) originally is an invocation of destruction. Here it is used figuratively to mean rebuke against this wish. It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar). ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ [Al-Qasas: 81], i.e., the home containing his wealth. ﴿The earth to swallow him and his home. And he had no company﴾ [Al-Qasas: 81], i.e., to repel the punishment from him: ﴿to support him against Allah﴾ [Al-Qasas: 81]. ﴿Nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾ [Al-Qasas: 81], i.e., through the strength of his own self and his wealth. ﴿And by morning, those who had wished to be in his place said, "Ah! Rather, Glorified is He, performs each of expansion and restriction purely by His will, not because of honor that necessitates expansion, nor because of humiliation that requires restriction. ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us﴾ [Al-Qasas: 82], i.e., by not granting us what we wished for: ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us﴾ [Al-Qasas: 82], i.e., just as He caused it to swallow him. ﴿Ah! It is as if the disbelievers never prosper﴾ [Al-Qasas: 82], i.e., for disregarding Allah's blessing by spending it other than in its proper way. Or, those who deny His messengers, deceived by their adornments.
