Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 28, verses 83–84:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[83–84] ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not seek exaltation on earth, nor corruption. And the good outcome is for the God-fearing.﴾ ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and whoever brings an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do.﴾ [al-Qasas: 84]

﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter, We assign it to those who do not seek exaltation on earth﴾, meaning domination and dominion through wrongdoing and arrogance; ﴿nor corruption﴾, meaning through oppression, transgression and barring from the way of God, exalted is He; ﴿and the good outcome﴾, meaning the praiseworthy end; ﴿is for the God-fearing﴾, meaning those who guard against what God, exalted is He, does not approve of in words and deeds.

Al-Zamakhshari, may God sanctify his spirit, said: The promise was not tied to abstaining from exaltation and corruption, but to abstaining from desiring them and from the inclination of hearts toward them, as He said: ﴿And do not incline toward those who do wrong﴾ [Hud: 113], so He tied the threat to inclining. It is related from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that a man may be pleased that the strap of his sandal is finer than the strap of his companion's sandal, and so he enters under this (verse).

It is related from al-Fudayl that he recited it and then said: "Wishful thinking has departed here." It is related from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he kept repeating it until he died. Some greedy people make exaltation belong to Pharaoh and corruption to Qarun, linking it to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾ [al-Qasas: 4] and ﴿And seek not corruption in the land﴾ [al-Qasas: 77], and they say: whoever is not like Pharaoh and Qarun, then for him is that Abode of the Hereafter. But they do not reflect upon His saying: ﴿And the good outcome is for the God-fearing﴾, as Ali, al-Fudayl and Umar, may God be pleased with them, reflected upon it. ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and whoever brings an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do﴾ [al-Qasas: 84]. Its meaning: "they will not be recompensed except..." etc. Thus the relative pronoun and the explicit noun were placed in the position of the pronoun, to censure their state by repeating the attribution of evil deeds to them, and this repetition makes evil deeds hateful to the hearts of the listeners. The meaning of His saying: ﴿except what they used to do﴾ [al-Qasas: 84] is: "its like." This is from His great grace and His vast generosity, that He does not recompense an evil deed except with its like, and recompenses a good deed tenfold and seven hundredfold. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿then for him is better than it﴾ [al-Qasas: 84], as stated in al-Kashshaf.

**The explanation of His words, may He be exalted:**

[85–86] ﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a return (ma'ad). Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in manifest error."﴾ ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 86]

﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an for you﴾, i.e., made it obligatory for you to recite it to the people, to convey it to them, and to proclaim it openly. ﴿Will surely bring you back﴾, i.e., after death, ﴿to a return (ma'ad)﴾, i.e., a great place of return. This is the praiseworthy station that He promised to raise you up in. Its indefiniteness (in ma'ad) is for glorification. Its rationale, as in (al-'Inaya) [a commentary by Akmal al-Din al-Babarti], is that the return (ma'ad) has become like a reality in the place of gathering (al-mahshar), because it is the beginning of returning to life and being restored to what one was. So He made his return great because of the greatness of his station therein.

Ibn Kathir said: "The return (ma'ad) is the Day of Resurrection. On it He will question him about what he was entrusted with of the burdens of prophethood, as He said: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 6], and He said: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What response did you receive?"﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 109], and He said: ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [Al-Zumar: 69]." Among the reports from Ibn 'Abbas there are several: "until the Day of Resurrection," "until death," and "until Paradise," which were related from him through several chains, as Ibn Kathir cited.

What al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn 'Abbas is that he said: "He will bring you back to Makkah as He brought you out of it." And from al-Dahhak, who said: "When the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah and reached al-Juhfah, he longed for Makkah, and this verse was revealed."

Ibn Kathir said: "This implies that this verse is Madani (revealed in Madinah), although the surah as a whole is Makki (revealed in Makkah). And Allah knows best."

Then he said: "The way to reconcile these statements is that Ibn 'Abbas explained it at one time as his return to Makkah, which is the conquest (al-fath), and which, according to Ibn 'Abbas, was near the approaching end of the Prophet's ﷺ life, just as Ibn 'Abbas explained the surah: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the conquest﴾ [Al-Nasr: 1] as meaning that it was the end of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was informed of it, and this took place in the presence of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who agreed with him and said: 'I know of it nothing other than what you know.' For this reason, Ibn 'Abbas at another time explained the words of Allah, ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾, as death. And at another time as the Day of Resurrection, which comes after death. And at another time as Paradise, which is his reward for conveying the message of Allah and delivering it to both species, the jinn and humankind (al-thaqalan). And because he is the most perfect of Allah's creation in absolute terms." End of quotation.

﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance"﴾, meaning himself, may he be honored, i.e., with what he deserves of reward. ﴿And who is in manifest error﴾, meaning the polytheists, i.e., with what they deserve of punishment. This sentence confirms the preceding threat.

﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you﴾ [Al-Qasas: 86], i.e., you did not think, before the revelation was sent down to you, that revelation would descend upon you. ﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ [Al-Qasas: 86], i.e., but it was cast upon you out of a mercy from your Lord. ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Qasas: 86], i.e., never be a helper to them. Rather, reject them and oppose them.

Al-Kirmani, in (al-Gharaib) [Gharaib al-Tafsir], related that its meaning is: "So do not be among them (bayna zahrani-him)," and that he was commanded to emigrate (hijrah).

(p-4733) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[87–88] ﴿And let them not turn you away from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And call to your Lord, and do not be among the polytheists. And do not invoke along with Allah another god. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]

﴿And let them not turn you away from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you﴾, i.e., from conveying them after their revelation. The command to proclaim them openly is because of the constraint of your breast due to their deception. For Allah is with you, elevating your word and supporting your religion. Therefore He said: ﴿And call to your Lord﴾, i.e., to worship Him alone, with no partner: ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾. ﴿And do not invoke along with Allah another god﴾ [al-Qasas: 88].

Al-Qadi said: This and what precedes it are for stirring up and cutting off the hopes of the polytheists of obtaining his support for them. That is, since it is not conceivable that he would do that, so as to be forbidden from it. So when He forbade him from supporting them and yielding to them, it is as if He said: that is hateful to Me, like polytheism, so do not be among those who do it. Or the intended meaning is the prohibition for his community, even though the address is to him ﷺ. Thus it is in (al-'Inayah).
